note: [L] proves the convergence of the normalized `ξ⁻¹ r⁴ J` to the free stress `T.J` for a kernel current produced by rank counting, not for the Haar average `T`. The display's factor `ξ_k/c_⋆` and the passage from `T` to `J` have no counterpart.

theorem produce_current (H : S.Hierarchy) (hW : W.Derivatives S) (ho : W.Orientation H.spin)
    (a : (Bel C.book).Hierarchy) (T : Lighthouse C.book) (hV : T.W.Derivatives (Bel C.book)) (p : T.W.Orientation a.spin)
    (hT : FreeDiv T a p) (X : Scaling S) (hp : Approaches (path X) (isoPanel X)) (h : Stable H.spin a.spin W T.W X) :
    ∃ J : KernelSpace H.spin,∃ Y : Scaling S,J.val ≠ 0 ∧ currentDiv W H.spin ho J=0 ∧
      Approaches (path Y) (isoPanel Y) ∧ Stable H.spin a.spin W T.W Y ∧ Y.meter J.val T.J := by

proof_context.conclusion: There is a nonzero divergence-free kernel current `J` and a stable scaling `Y` with `Y.meter J.val T.J`, i.e. `balanced_J Y J → T.J`.

snippet.text: def balanced_J (X : Scaling S) (J : S.Stress) (k : ℕ) : (Bel C.book).Stress := (X.xi k)⁻¹ • labelScale X k J

proof_context.conclusion: `balanced_J X J k = (X.xi k)⁻¹ • labelScale X k J` is the `ξ⁻¹ r⁴ J` pulled back by the frame.
